stem: At this rate, how many hours did the worker work last week?
stimulus: A temporary staffing agency pays a data-entry worker $24 per hour. Last week, the worker earned a total of $840 from this job.
explanation: You know the total ($840) and the rate ($24 per hour), and you need the time. Time = total ÷ rate, so 840 dollars ÷ 24 dollars/hour = 35 hours. The dollars cancel and hours are left, which tells you the setup is right.

B.why: You subtracted the hourly rate from the total earnings (840 − 24). Subtracting a rate from a total gives no meaningful quantity, and the units do not cancel to hours.

C.why: You added the hourly rate to the total earnings (840 + 24). Dollars per hour cannot be added to dollars. You need to divide.

D.why: You multiplied the total by the rate (840 × 24) when the units say to divide. Your result would be in dollars squared per hour, not hours.

stem: How many inches of water were in the gauge at the end of the storm?
stimulus: A hydrologist checks a rain gauge that already holds 1.5 inches of water. A storm then adds rain at a constant rate of 0.4 inch per hour for 6 hours. No water leaves the gauge during the storm.
explanation: The storm adds 0.4 inch/hour × 6 hours = 2.4 inches. The gauge already held 1.5 inches, so at the end it holds 1.5 + 2.4 = 3.9 inches.

A.why: You subtracted the starting 1.5 inches from the storm's 2.4 inches. The storm adds water to the gauge, so you should have added the two amounts.

B.why: 2.4 inches is only the rain the storm added. You stopped before adding the 1.5 inches that were already in the gauge.

D.why: You divided 6 hours by 0.4 inch per hour (getting 15) and then added 1.5. Hours ÷ (inches/hour) doesn't give inches. Rate × time does.

stem: What is the greatest number of athletes who can each receive at least 450 milliliters of the drink?
stimulus: A sports scientist mixes 4,000 milliliters of an electrolyte drink for a training session. Each athlete must receive at least 450 milliliters of the drink.
explanation: Number of athletes = total ÷ amount per athlete = 4,000 mL ÷ 450 mL/athlete ≈ 8.9. Only whole athletes count, and each one needs at least 450 mL, so round down to 8. Eight athletes use 3,600 mL, and a ninth would push the total past 4,000 mL.

B.why: You rounded 8.9 up to 9. Nine athletes would need 9 × 450 = 4,050 mL, which is more than the 4,000 mL available. For a 'greatest number' question you must round down.

C.why: You subtracted one athlete's share from the total (4,000 − 450). That is the drink left after serving one athlete, not the number of athletes.

D.why: You multiplied the total by the amount per athlete when the units say to divide. mL × mL/athlete doesn't give a count of athletes.

stem: At this rate, how many more hours will it take the annotator to finish tagging the corpus?
stimulus: A linguist hires an annotator to tag every word of a 9,000-word corpus by part of speech. The annotator works at a constant rate of 450 words per hour and has already tagged 3,600 of the words.
explanation: The words left to tag are 9,000 − 3,600 = 5,400. Time = words ÷ rate = 5,400 words ÷ 450 words/hour = 12 hours.

A.why: 3,600 ÷ 450 = 8 is the number of hours the annotator has already worked. The question asks how much time is left.

C.why: 9,000 ÷ 450 = 20 is the time for the whole corpus. You didn't remove the 3,600 words that are already tagged.

D.why: You added the tagged words to the corpus size (9,000 + 3,600) instead of subtracting them, so you counted the completed work as extra work still to do.

stem: What is the total cost, in dollars, for the researcher's order?
stimulus: A folklore archive charges $4 per page to copy handwritten collections of village tales, plus a one-time handling fee of $10 per order. A researcher orders copies of 23 pages.
explanation: The page charge is $4/page × 23 pages = $92. Add the one-time $10 fee: 92 + 10 = $102.

A.why: You subtracted the $10 handling fee from the page charge. The fee is added to the cost, not taken off.

B.why: $92 is only the page charge. You stopped before adding the $10 handling fee.

D.why: You added the $10 fee to every page ($14 × 23). The fee is charged once per order, not once per page.

stem: At these rates, how many more centimeters will colony A grow than colony B over a period of 15 years?
stimulus: A marine biologist monitors two colonies of branching coral on the same reef. Colony A grows at a constant rate of 1.2 centimeters per year, and colony B grows at a constant rate of 0.8 centimeter per year.
explanation: Colony A grows 1.2 cm/year × 15 years = 18 cm, and colony B grows 0.8 cm/year × 15 years = 12 cm. The difference is 18 − 12 = 6 cm. You can also find (1.2 − 0.8) × 15 = 6 directly.

B.why: 12 cm is colony B's growth over 15 years. The question asks for the difference between the two colonies.

C.why: 18 cm is colony A's total growth. You stopped before subtracting colony B's 12 cm.

D.why: You added the two colonies' growth (18 + 12). 'How many more' asks for a difference, not a combined total.

stem: At this tempo, how many minutes does it take the ensemble to play the movement?
stimulus: A musicologist studying a Baroque dance counts 360 beats in one movement. An ensemble performs the movement at a constant tempo of 120 beats per minute.
explanation: Time = beats ÷ tempo = 360 beats ÷ 120 beats/minute = 3 minutes. The beats cancel and minutes are left.

A.why: You divided the tempo by the number of beats (120 ÷ 360) instead of the other way round. The units come out as 1/minute, not minutes.

C.why: You subtracted the tempo from the number of beats (360 − 120). Beats per minute can't be subtracted from beats.

D.why: You multiplied the beats by the tempo when the units say to divide. The result would be in beats squared per minute, not minutes.

stem: How many samples did the seismometer record while the ground was shaking?
stimulus: A seismometer records ground motion at a constant rate of 40 samples per second. During a small earthquake, the ground shook for 1 minute 15 seconds, and the seismometer recorded throughout the shaking.
explanation: First write the duration in seconds: 1 minute 15 seconds = 60 + 15 = 75 seconds. Then total = rate × time = 40 samples/second × 75 seconds = 3,000 samples.

A.why: You divided the time by the rate (75 ÷ 40) when the units say to multiply. Seconds ÷ (samples/second) doesn't give a number of samples.

B.why: You treated 1 minute as 1 second and multiplied 40 by 1 + 15 = 16. Convert the minute to 60 seconds before you multiply.

C.why: You used only the 1 minute (40 × 60) and left out the extra 15 seconds of shaking.
